extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of advertising/media history; readers interested in historical newspaper practices
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and evaluating the conventions, rules, and criteria used in historical matrimonial advertisements and matchmaking agencies as reported in a history of advertising. Focuses on procedural rules, applicant/describer conventions, fee structures, privacy/access, and the kinds of attributes sought in ads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managers' ethical conduct and secrecy
rubrics_metrics.description: the most upright Conduct, greatest Delicacy and inviolable Secrecy shall be observed in all their Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers advertise their establishment as founded on 'honourable' principles intended to promote happiness and to put a stop to deceptive advertisements; they publicly assure probity as a selling/quality point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and candour of applicants' descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Such as cannot attend in Person, are requested to signify their Intention by their Friend in Writing; it is hoped and presumed that such Recital will be made with the utmost Exactness; and not only the Situation in Life, but the Age, Constitution, and Religion of the Party set forth with all possible Accuracy and Candour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies require detailed, accurate written statements (age, social position, physical constitution, religion, etc.) from principals or their agents; accurate descriptions are treated as essential to matchmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and payment terms
rubrics_metrics.description: the Terms upon which this truly important Matter is commenced, is no more than Five Guineas, to be paid to the Managers on taking down the Minutes of the Business; and no more is to be paid till after the Matter is completed ... the Payment of five Guineas has been thought by some too much ... reduced ... to two Guineas ... Ladies of Reputation are invited gratis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies specify upfront fees, staged payment (initial fee then none until completion), occasional refunds/price reductions to appease complaints, and free entry for certain categories (e.g., 'ladies of reputation'); some also advertise lending of large sums on equitable terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of agents/proxies and proxy courtship
rubrics_metrics.description: Courtships may be carried on by Way of Proxy ... Such as cannot attend in Person, are requested to signify their Intention by their Friend in Writing ... agents shall have been apprised that the Terms ... is no more than Five Guineas
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies accept and expect representation by friends/agents; agents must be informed of terms and provide accurate information on behalf of principals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and separate interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Person who appears at Dover Street (aforesaid) will be shown into a separate Apartment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews are conducted in separate rooms to protect 'delicacy' and prevent idle curiosity; parties do not see each other until a meeting is finally and satisfactorily arranged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hours of access and accessibility accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proprietors are to be spoken with from eleven in the Morning till four in the Afternoon, and from seven in the Evening till ten at Night ... every Day, Sunday excepted
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies set explicit visiting/interview hours (including evening hours) to accommodate busy clients (e.g., gentlemen in court/city).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity to printed rules; no deviation allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: The negotiations are conducted in conformity with printed rules, from which not the slightest deviation will be allowed ... The rules are to be published for ten shillings — the price is set upon them for no other reason than as some guard against the thoughtless, the idle or the ill disposed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies publish formal rules (for a fee) and enforce them strictly as both a procedural safeguard and a filter against unserious or malicious applicants; possession of the rules may entitle to expedited service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber classification system (class descriptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of subscription to be regulated according to the class in which they place themselves, the classes being described thus in the plan: [lists of Ladies 1st-5th Class and Gentlemen 1st-5th Class with age, fortune, education, disposition, occupation, health etc.]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies categorize subscribers into discrete classes (with example templates for each) defining age, fortune, profession, health, disposition and social attributes; subscribers self-describe into classes and receive lists of potential matches accordingly; managers assist if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and correspondence protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters must be post paid, and addressed to O. P. Q., Two-penny Post-office ... real names and addresses will be considered a pledge of sincerity ... Address, Poste Restante a Paris
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ads and agencies insist on specific addressing methods (post-paid letters, Poste Restante), often request real names/addresses or cartes-de-visite as a pledge of sincerity, and set clear reply channels to control responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principals-only and seriousness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: None but Principals will be treated with, nor need any apply that are deficient in any one Particular ... it is earnestly solicited that no one will reply to it from curiosity or amusement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many advertisements explicitly restrict replies to principals (not agents or curiosity-seekers) and warn that curiously motivated responses will be disregarded; some ads require meeting every listed particular to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical selection criteria sought in matrimonial advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ad examples specify required qualities: age ranges (e.g., 18–25), fortune thresholds (e.g., not less than £5,000 or incomes of £400/£500 a year), physical attributes (height, complexion, teeth), moral and domestic qualities (education, economy, not too talkative, keeps secrets, charitable disposition), social rank/profession exclusions (except Church/Army/Navy), acceptance of children or widowhood, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual advertisers commonly enumerate a mix of economic (fortune/income), demographic (age, height), physical (skin, teeth), social (education, family rank), moral/temperamental (charitable, domestic habits), and practical (can keep house, tolerate children) criteria; ads vary from romantic to mercenary in emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of publicity and 'news' framing (puffery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mrs Cornelys ... her advertisements usually appeared as news paragraphs ... she seems to have thoroughly understood the advantages of judicious puffery
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisers and managers use news-like paragraphs, handbills, masking/entertainments, printed prospectuses and portfolios to publicize services and create social cachet; presentation as news or testimonial material functions as a promotional technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and inspection of candidate portfolios
rubrics_metrics.description: The Portfolio ... containing letters from gentlemen in every sphere of life, possessing property from £400 to £3000 per annum, and may be purchased or inspected by ladies, free of charge, at the agent's
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies assemble portfolios/listings of candidates that prospective clients can inspect (sometimes for a fee or free to certain clients) as part of matchmaking; access policies are specified in ads.
